findings.finding: The confirmed outer-lock self-deadlock in `run_repair` (holding the tracker write lock across the repair loop while each inner `append_event` re-acquires it) is being shipped as-is, with the fix deferred to a follow-up. The plan captures the analysis in plan prose, but specifies no in-code marker — no TODO/FIXME comment, no disabled outer-lock, no follow-up ticket reference in `link_audit.py` — so a future contributor reading the shipped code will see the outer `lock.acquire()` call and not know it is a known self-deadlock that makes `--repair` hang.
findings.location: Scope → `src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py`; plan section 'On the outer lock — a confirmed defect, deferred to a follow-up'
scenarios: A future contributor adds a new repair command, copies the `run_repair` outer-lock pattern from `link_audit.py` as a template, and introduces the same deadlock.

A contributor profiling `--repair` slowness doesn't know the outer lock is the culprit and spends time elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix:
In `src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py`, immediately above the outer `with lock.write_lock():` (or equivalent `lock.acquire()`) call in `run_repair`, add:
```python
# KNOWN DEFECT (follow-up <ticket-id>): holding the store write-lock across the
# repair loop causes a self-deadlock — inner append_event re-acquires the same
# flock. Per-write locking (as in fsck_repair) is the fix. Until then, --repair
# will hang on the first write. Use the incremental driver as a workaround.
```
Also add the follow-up ticket ID to the Scope bullet for `link_audit.py`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the `--repair` self-deadlock before shipping: either drop the outer `lock.acquire` and let each `append_event` take the lock independently (matching `fsck_repair`'s per-write pattern), or make this ticket's scope include the fix rather than deferring it, so `--repair` is operable in a live store when this ticket lands.
evidence: Plan: 'a real `--repair` run against this repository's own tracker completed ZERO of 18 findings in 10 minutes. Slow pushes would have landed some; zero progress is the signature of blocking on the first write.'

`run_repair` acquires `lock.acquire(tracker, …)` at line 234, then `repair_finding` → `add_dependency` → `_write_link_event` → `_seam.append_event` → `write_and_push` → `stage_and_commit` → `_lock.write_lock(tracker, dual_window=True)` tries to re-acquire the same lock.
Plan: 'The remedy is to acquire per write rather than across the loop, as `fsck_repair` does by batching. It is tracked as follow-up work and is NOT part of this ticket.'
Tests pass only because the graph test fixture stubs the real store write path, so the inner `write_lock` is never entered in tests.
findings.finding: `run_repair` holds the outer `lock.acquire` handle across its repair loop while every inner write re-acquires the same dual-window lock via `stage_and_commit` → `_lock.write_lock`, causing a self-deadlock: the mkdir leg raises `FileExistsError`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` sees the same live PID and refuses to reclaim, so `--repair` completes zero repairs in a live store. The plan acknowledges this empirically (0/18 findings repaired, 10 minutes) and defers the fix, but the shipped implementation cannot achieve its stated goal.
findings.location: Approach section — 'On the outer lock — a confirmed defect, deferred to a follow-up'; `src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:233-243` (`run_repair`)
scenarios: Any live `rebar link-audit --repair` invocation against a real tracker hangs indefinitely on the first write, repairing nothing.
A CI run using the real store (not the test fixture stub) would also deadlock.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the outer `lock.acquire` / `handle.release` from `run_repair` and write the pre-tag outside any lock (it is a git tag, not a store event). Each `repair_finding` call will then let `add_dependency` and `_unlink_edge` take the lock independently per write, exactly as `fsck_repair._repair_ticket` does. The reconciler-in-flight check and pre-tag can remain at the top of `run_repair` before the loop.

findings.finding: The leaf plan discloses a confirmed self-deadlock in `--repair` (the outer write lock blocks every inner write, yielding zero completions in 10 minutes) and defers the fix to follow-up work. The parent story's success criterion states blocking edges must be 'repairable in a single pass,' but the leaf's shipped `--repair` code path cannot complete even one repair due to the deadlock — the actual repair was done with a separate workaround driver, not with `rebar link-audit --repair`.
findings.location: Approach section — 'On the outer lock — a confirmed defect, deferred to a follow-up'
scenarios: An operator runs `rebar link-audit --repair` on a store with stale edges and waits indefinitely, receiving no output, because the command deadlocks on its first write.
The follow-up fix is never delivered, and `rebar link-audit --repair` permanently fails to repair anything — violating the parent's repairability criterion.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the lock acquisition from the outer repair loop to the per-write level (matching `fsck_repair`'s batching pattern), which is the fix already described in the plan's 'On the outer lock' section. This makes the deadlock finding moot without requiring a separate follow-up ticket.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a rollback procedure to the plan (e.g. `git reset --hard pre-link-audit-repair`) and explicitly assert the post-rollback event-store state — confirming that all repair events written after the tag OID are cleanly absent and the store is consistent after the reset.
evidence: 'the pre-tag is the answer to re-resolution being a best-effort reconstruction: an individual edge's original intent is unrecoverable, but the run as a whole is'
The plan never states: what command a user runs to roll back (e.g. `git reset --hard pre-link-audit-repair`), nor confirms whether that leaves the event store in the exact pre-run state.

ABSENCE: no description of post-rollback event-store state — specifically whether events appended after the pre-tag OID but before a mid-run failure are simply absent after a hard reset, or whether compensating forward-events are needed.
findings.finding: The plan specifies that a `pre-link-audit-repair` git tag is created before any writes to enable rollback, but does not define what the rollback procedure actually is, nor does it assert the state of the event store AFTER a rollback is executed. The T11 rubric requires the plan to assert on the schema/store STATE after rollback — not merely that a recovery artifact exists.
findings.location: Approach section — '**`--repair` reuses `fsck --repair`'s safety envelope...**'; AC line '`--repair` force-writes the `pre-link-audit-repair` tag...'
scenarios: A repair run partially completes (e.g. 5 of 18 findings repaired), then fails hard. The operator wants to roll back. The pre-tag exists, but the plan gives no guidance on how to use it and does not assert that `git reset --hard pre-link-audit-repair` leaves the store fully consistent (no orphaned LINK events referencing tickets correctly, etc.).
A rollback exits 0 via `git reset --hard` but leaves the working tree or index in an unexpected state if the store has uncommitted partial writes, which the plan does not rule out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a subsection under the repair safety envelope: 'To roll back: `git reset --hard pre-link-audit-repair`. This resets the tracker branch to its pre-run HEAD, discarding all LINK/UNLINK events written by the repair run. Because every repair write is a committed git event, no partial write can exist outside the git history; the store is fully consistent at the tag OID after the reset. If the tag has been re-pointed by a subsequent repair attempt, use `git reflog` to find the original OID.' Also add an AC: 'After `git reset --hard pre-link-audit-repair`, the event-file count equals the pre-run count and a subsequent `rebar link-audit` reproduces the original finding list.'

findings.finding: The final AC (live-run scan of this repository's tracker) lacks the `[operator-attested]` tag but requires manual verification against the live tracker state. Its proving 'command' is described only in prose ('checking, for every remaining finding, the status of the endpoint … asserting each is closed') with no concrete command or script, making it neither deterministic nor in-session completable as a standard AC.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — last AC ('rebar link-audit --output json against this repository's own tracker reports zero findings that can affect scheduling')
findings.suggested_fix: Tag the AC `[operator-attested]`: prefix with `[operator-attested]` and add: 'attested by a comment on this ticket showing (a) the tracker HEAD OID the scan ran against, (b) the JSON output of `rebar link-audit --output json`, and (c) for each remaining finding with a non-closed blocked-side, a note explaining why it is inert.' This matches the pattern already used for the pre-repair finding-count AC.

findings.finding: The plan's description of the ambiguous-pair detection mechanism does not match the implementation. The plan states 'the driver counts the pair's net-active links; when that count is not exactly 1 the finding is reported unrepairable with reason ambiguous-pair', but the actual implementation uses _unlink_would_cancel (link_audit.py:83–98) which retrieves the relation that UNLINK would cancel and compares it against the relation being repaired. These two mechanisms are not equivalent: a pair with exactly 1 net-active link of the wrong relation (e.g., a relates_to that was written after a now-stale depends_on) passes a count-of-1 check but correctly fails the relation-comparison check. The plan's description understates the protection the code actually provides and would confuse a reviewer auditing the ambiguous-pair logic.
findings.location: Approach section, 'Ambiguous pairs are never repaired' paragraph
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'Before repairing any edge, the driver counts the pair's net-active links; when that count is not exactly 1 the finding is reported unrepairable with reason ambiguous-pair and left untouched' with: 'Before repairing any edge, the driver asks which relation the next UNLINK on this ordered pair would cancel (the most-recent net-active link, via _get_link_info); when that relation does not match the blocking relation being repaired the finding is reported unrepairable with reason ambiguous-pair and left untouched.'

findings.finding: The `run_repair` outer lock (`lock.acquire()` holding both the fcntl and mkdir legs) deadlocks with the inner lock taken by every `append_event` → `write_and_push` → `stage_and_commit` → `write_lock()` call: the mkdir leg (`os.mkdir(.ticket-write.lock.d)`) sees `FileExistsError`, `_mkdir_lock_is_stale` finds the same PID alive and returns False, so it spins for the full 60-second budget then raises `LockTimeout` (converted to `CommandError` by `_seam.append_event`). Every `repair_finding` call is therefore marked `unrepairable` after a 60s wait, making `--repair` non-functional in production. The existing tests escape this because they invoke `repair_finding()` directly rather than through `run_repair()`, so no test exercises the outer-lock + inner-append path.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Repair writes LINK BEFORE UNLINK'; `run_repair` in `src/rebar/_commands/link_audit.py:223-245`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single outer lock in `run_repair` with per-finding lock acquire/release (matching `fsck_repair._repair_ticket`'s pattern): take the lock, do ONE write (link or unlink), release it, reacquire for the next write. This is the established pattern in the codebase, avoids mkdir re-entrancy, and each write's atomicity is preserved by the seam's own lock.

findings.finding: The AC includes a criterion ("A plain `rebar link-audit` does not trigger a store reconverge; verified by asserting `ensure_initialized` is called with `init_only=True` when `--repair` is absent") but the Testing section enumerates no corresponding test case, creating a gap between what the AC demands and what the test module is spec'd to contain.
findings.location: AC: 'A plain rebar link-audit does not trigger a store reconverge; verified by asserting ensure_initialized is called with init_only=True'; Testing section (no corresponding entry)

findings.finding: The AC criterion for the `pre-link-audit-repair` tag ("force-writes the tag at the tracker's pre-run OID before its first write, and a second `--repair` run re-points it rather than failing; verified by asserting the tag OID in the repair test and re-running repair") is not explicitly enumerated as a test case in the Testing section, leaving the "repair test" as the implicit host without stating what it must additionally assert.
findings.location: AC: 'pre-link-audit-repair tag... verified by asserting the tag OID in the repair test and re-running repair'; Testing section: 'Happy path: --repair on a store with one ancestor-blocking edge removes it'

findings.finding: The reconciler-in-flight abort is named as an explicit safety mechanism ('abort before any write if a reconciler pass is in flight') but has no corresponding test case in the Testing section and no AC line that verifies it. If `_reconciler_in_flight` returns true, the run should abort with a user-visible message and a non-zero exit code; this behaviour is unverified and the user-facing error output (message text, exit code) is unspecified.
findings.location: Approach section: 'abort before any write if a reconciler pass is in flight'; Testing section (no matching test case); AC items (no matching item)
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Testing: 'Failure: `--repair` when `_reconciler_in_flight` returns true exits non-zero, emits an error message naming the in-flight reconciler, and writes zero events; asserted by monkeypatching `_reconciler_in_flight` to return True and comparing the event-file count before and after.' Add a matching AC item.

findings.finding: The leaf unilaterally weakens the parent's 'empty second pass' AC without updating the parent first. The parent story (affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12) requires that `rebar link-audit` reports an empty second pass after repair. The leaf's final AC amends this to allow 8 residual findings (closed-source mis-escalated edges) and declares the original criterion 'unreachable,' but does not update the parent AC. Under the conflict rule the parent's criterion is authoritative; the leaf diverges from it.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — final bullet (the live-repo scan criterion, amended from 'zero outstanding findings, exits 0')
findings.suggested_fix: Update parent story affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12's AC to read: '`rebar link-audit` run twice against this repository's own tracker reports a non-empty first pass; after `--repair`, all remaining findings have a closed ticket on the blocked side and are therefore inert to scheduling.' Then re-attest the parent's plan review. Only after the parent is corrected does the leaf's amended AC become a consistent narrowing.

findings.finding: The plan describes a specific failure path — `--repair` detects a reconciler pass is in-flight and aborts before any write — but the Testing section and ACs contain no test case that exercises or asserts this behaviour, leaving an uncovered failure path for a newly-introduced safety envelope.
findings.location: Testing section / Acceptance Criteria / Approach §'--repair MIRRORS the safety envelope'
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section, add: 'Failure: `--repair` while a reconciler pass is in flight writes zero events and exits non-zero; asserted by monkeypatching the in-flight check to return True and comparing event-file counts before and after.' Add a corresponding AC line.

findings.finding: The leaf's amended live-run AC contradicts the parent story's explicit acceptance criterion. The parent (affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12) states: '`rebar link-audit` run twice against this repository's own tracker reports a non-empty first pass and an empty second pass after its repair.' The leaf's final AC instead accepts 8 residual findings on the second pass (argued inert) and explicitly states 'the literal zero outstanding findings criterion is NOT met.' This is a parent-AC contradiction — the leaf redefines the criterion the parent uses to declare the story done rather than narrowing it.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — last AC bullet ('rebar link-audit --output json against this repository's own tracker reports zero findings that can affect scheduling…'); parent ticket affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12 AC bullet 3
findings.suggested_fix: Update parent affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12 AC 3 to read: '`rebar link-audit` run against this repository's own tracker reports a non-empty first pass; after repair, any residual findings on a second pass are verified to be inert (all blocking-side endpoints are closed, so no residual can distort `ready` or `next-batch`).' This realigns the parent to the amended understanding, forces parent re-review, and removes the contradiction.
